limitations: Discord requires verification for bots joining over 100 servers (guilds). Standard user OAuth2 does not require manual review.

assumptions: Developer has active Discord account with 2FA enabled
Configuring standard OAuth2 code grant with identify and email scopes

externalWait.publishedRange: Instant activation (no review required for standard user OAuth2)

prerequisites.text: Discord user account with 2-Factor Authentication enabled

steps.title: Create Application in Discord Developer Portal
steps.instructions: Navigate to the Discord Developer Portal at `https://discord.com/developers/applications`. Log in, click 'New Application', give your app a name, and accept the Developer Terms of Service.
steps.completionCheck: Application overview displays Client ID (Snowflake ID).

steps.title: Configure OAuth2 Redirect URLs
steps.instructions: In the left sidebar, navigate to 'OAuth2' > 'General'. Under 'Redirects', click 'Add Redirect' and enter your exact callback URL (e.g., `https://app.example.com/api/auth/callback/discord`). Discord requires exact URL matching including scheme, host, and path. Click 'Save Changes'.

steps.title: Generate Client Secret & Save Credentials
steps.instructions: Under 'Client Information', find 'Client Secret' and click 'Reset Secret'. Copy the secret immediately to your secure backend environment variables (`DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET`). Discord will not show this value again.
steps.completionCheck: Client secret copied to secrets manager.

steps.title: Construct Authorization URL & Scopes
steps.instructions: Build your authorization request URL targeting `https://discord.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id={CLIENT_ID}&response_type=code&redirect_uri={ENCODED_REDIRECT}&scope=identify%20email`. Use `identify` for basic user info and `email` for verified email address.
steps.completionCheck: User consent prompt displays requested scopes.

claims.text: Discord applications are created at https://discord.com/developers/applications and identified by a snowflake Client ID.
Discord OAuth2 redirect URLs require exact string matching; wildcards and insecure HTTP schemes (except localhost) are rejected.
Client secrets can be reset at any time and must be handled as confidential backend credentials.
Standard user identification requires 'identify' and optional 'email' scopes.
